title: cc-fires-its-clock-probes-on-its-own-pulse
intention: The cc device fires its own clock probes (memory_curve, is_the_memory_curve_recorded) from its groundloop/pulse.py on each heartbeat, so they run again now that the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/.
why: Since bae622881f03 PROVED (2026-09-30) the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/ folders; it calls only groundloop/pulse.py files. So memory_curve, is_the_memory_curve_recorded are dark: the only firing left is one pass at web-server start through bus_client's private GroundLoopDevice, which ticket efb670ff1dd8 removes. That is the lived symptom: memory_curve samples the CC scope's cgroup memory.current and per-process RSS into a durable series each firing; is_the_memory_curve_recorded watches that the series exists and covers a whole session (ticket the-memory-curve-is-recorded-not-eyeballed), and nobody is looking. The same folder holds a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.py and the_shim_delivers_mail.py, which are event probes (group 3) and must NOT fire on the beat.
traces_to: Law 6 and Law 1 via ticket bae622881f03 (PROVED 2026-09-30): the heartbeat calls each groundloop/pulse.py and nothing else, and Akien ruled clock probes are 'tickled by the system device or their owning devices (from the ground loop pulse)'. The owner fires its own watch.
how: Compose the shared tool cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py built by ticket 32959e65ec5a (do not copy its logic). write cairn/devices/cc/groundloop/pulse.py: a module-level BeatProbes('cc', <this folder>, ['memory_curve', 'is_the_memory_curve_recorded'], bus) and on_pulse(now, context) returning its pulse record. Only the named probes fire; The same folder holds a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.py and the_shim_delivers_mail.py, which are event probes (group 3) and must NOT fire on the beat. The probe files stay where they are, unchanged.
falsifier: Proof cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py: (1) discovery.pulse_sites() lists cairn/devices/cc/groundloop/pulse.py at class level; (2) the module's BeatProbes names exactly ['memory_curve', 'is_the_memory_curve_recorded'] and each resolves to a Probe; (3) other modules in cairn/devices/cc/probes/ are not in its roster; (4) on_pulse(now, {}) with a recording stub bus returns a record whose fired+held entries cover exactly those probes. Live horizon: three consecutive beats of ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json list the cc trigger ok. Wrong intent if one of these probes turns out to be event-driven rather than clock-driven.
watchme: none, because the probes being moved ARE the watches (cairn/devices/cc/probes/memory_curve.py, cairn/devices/cc/probes/is_the_memory_curve_recorded.py), each keeping its own ticket's WATCHME, and whether they fire is read on every beat in the heartbeat's own record ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json (the cc trigger's ok flag and pulse record).
assumption_check: (1) memory_curve, is_the_memory_curve_recorded are clock probes (Akien's group-2 list, 2026-09-30). (2) The heartbeat calls on_pulse(now, {}) once per 60s beat and holds the module between beats, re-loading it when cairn/devices/cc/groundloop/pulse.py changes, which resets crossing memory; a reset re-pokes a still-true condition once, which is acceptable and matches a loop restart under the old runner. (3) A probe's poke needs a bus; connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False) gives one without beating. (4) The probe files are unchanged; only who fires them moves.
missing_check: (a) This depends on 32959e65ec5a (the shared cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py); it waits at BUILDME until that is PROVED. (b) The same folder holds a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.py and the_shim_delivers_mail.py, which are event probes (group 3) and must NOT fire on the beat.
builder_check: WHERE: new cairn/devices/cc/groundloop/pulse.py and new cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py. HOW: from cairn.tools.base.beat_probes import BeatProbes; module level _PROBES = BeatProbes('cc', Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], ['memory_curve', 'is_the_memory_curve_recorded'], bus=<lazy connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False)>); on_pulse(now, context) returns _PROBES.on_pulse(now, context). The helper's exact constructor is whatever 32959e65ec5a built: read cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py first. TESTS use a stub bus and never fire the real triggers (the census/DB reads are slow); assert the roster, not the firing, which the helper's own proof covers. DO NOT move or edit the probe files.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient 50c3d772637c .. validate fa0941a84e0d, each learned)

decisions.text: The proof is written and committed red at b690c7d7: cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py, the same FAILURES/ok() pattern as cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py (module-level FAILURES; ok(name, passed, detail) prints '  ok   <name>' or '  RED  <name>' and appends on a fail, never raises; main() returns 1 if FAILURES else 0). It loads the pulse by path inside the teeth and reads FIRER.roster(), FIRER.probes(), FIRER.bind(stub) and on_pulse; the builder writes only the pulse and must not edit the proof.

Create cairn/devices/cc/groundloop/pulse.py (no __init__.py; the heartbeat loads it by path) mirroring cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py: a docstring naming this ticket; 'from pathlib import Path'; 'from cairn.tools.base.beat_probes import BeatProbes'; NAMES = ('memory_curve', 'is_the_memory_curve_recorded'); def _bus(): from cairn.tools.bus_client import reach; return reach()  (imported lazily, called with no devices because no named probe asks over the bus; BeatProbes calls it on the first beat, never at import); FIRER = BeatProbes('cc', Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent, list(NAMES), bus=_bus); def on_pulse(now, context=None) -> dict: return FIRER.on_pulse(now, context).

After the build commit the running heartbeat reloads on its own (Triggers holds pulse modules by mtime). Read ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json on three consecutive beats (last_run advancing each time, one pid): the 'cc' class-level trigger is listed ok true each time. 'cairn groundloop status' prints the same record.
